symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each input integer.
symbols.quote: Power-saving integer multiplication is the main result: for $n$, the number of bits in each input, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$, the exponent saved from the power of $\lg n$, a fixed Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, which is $o(n\log n)$, so it refutes the [Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture](conjecture.md) in this model.

symbols.name: power-saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent $2^{-182}$ saved from the power of $\lg n$.
symbols.quote: Power-saving integer multiplication is the main result: for $n$, the number of bits in each input, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$, the exponent saved from the power of $\lg n$, a fixed Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, which is $o(n\log n)$, so it refutes the [Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture](conjecture.md) in this model.

symbols.name: coefficient precision
symbols.meaning: The number of bits of precision of each stored coefficient.
symbols.quote: Let $p$ be the number of bits of precision of each stored coefficient, of order $\lg n$, and $V=\Theta(n)$ the volume of stored data.

symbols.name: data volume
symbols.meaning: The volume of stored data, of order $n$.
symbols.quote: Let $p$ be the number of bits of precision of each stored coefficient, of order $\lg n$, and $V=\Theta(n)$ the volume of stored data.

relations.quote: Power-saving integer multiplication is the main result: for $n$, the number of bits in each input, and $\kappa=2^{-182}$, the exponent saved from the power of $\lg n$, a fixed Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, which is $o(n\log n)$, so it refutes the [Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture](conjecture.md) in this model.

The exact $2n$-bit product follows from radix digits, the Chinese-remainder address map, two forward transforms, a pointwise product, the opposite transform, rescaling, rounding and carry propagation, with total error below $1/2$, as set out in [The multiplication algorithm](multiplication-algorithm.md).
This slack also covers any fixed power of $\log p$, so the total time is bounded by $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$, as [Cost accounting and the exponent κ](cost-accounting.md) shows.
